**CLASS**: claim-drift / **ORIGINAL** (L14–15): "chose the Faculty of Medicine I don’t remember on what grounds" / **REVISION** (L13): "chose the Faculty of Medicine on good grounds" / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: An admission of forgotten, arbitrary motive is reversed into a claim of deliberate good reason — the opposite proposition.

**CLASS**: claim-drift / **ORIGINAL** (L13): "I had at the time only a slight idea of the Faculties in general" / **REVISION** (L12): "I had an idea of the Faculties in general" / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: The stated ignorance ("only a slight", "at the time") is neutralised; the reader can no longer see that the choice of medicine was made without understanding of the alternatives.

**CLASS**: dropped-qualification / **ORIGINAL** (L20–23): "Not counting reviews, feuilletons, paragraphs, and all that I have written from day to day for the newspapers, which it would be difficult now to seek out and collect," / **REVISION**: absent / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: The exclusion that scopes the output figure, plus the existence of an uncollected body of journalism; the reader now rea

**CLASS**: claim-drift / **ORIGINAL** (L23): "published more than three hundred signatures of print" / **REVISION** (L19): "published three hundred signatures of print" / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: A lower bound becomes an exact figure; the reader can no longer tell the true total exceeds three hundred.

**CLASS**: claim-drift / **ORIGINAL** (L30–31): "it is probably due to my close association with medicine that I have succeeded in avoiding many mistakes" / **REVISION** (L26): "it is due to my close association with medicine that I have succeeded in avoiding many mistakes" / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: The hedge "probably" — a tentative causal attribution is stated as established cause.

**CLASS**: claim-drift / **ORIGINAL** (L26): "I have no doubt that the study of medicine has had an important influence on my literary work" / **REVISION** (L22): "The study of medicine has had an important influence on my literary work" / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: The first-person attribution; a personal conviction is restated as impersonal fact, and the reader can no longer see it as the writer

**CLASS**: dropped-fact / **ORIGINAL** (L7–8): "On a separate sheet I send a few facts, very bald, but I can do no more...." / **REVISION** (L7): "On a separate sheet I send the facts." / **WHAT THE READER LOSES**: That the enclosure is a few bald facts and the limit of what the writer will supply; "the facts" reads as a full account, removing the reluctance the paragraph exists to state.

_how: One entry per transcript. `note` and `annotation` are the operator's; both may stay empty.
The nulls are the two contract counts, and they are counts of what the findings quoted
under `_findings_to_review` DO — not of what the critic says it did. Read the transcript.
Nothing here is derived for you, because a critic grading its own compliance is the
failure verify-run.mjs was written to close. collect refuses to run until they are numbers.
